context_documents.title: What an articulated arm and a handoff actually cost
context_documents.body:
# 2023-6328: What an articulated arm and a handoff actually cost

Version: February controls write-up, May wiring report and pinned repository snapshot; event binary unverified

## Evidence premises

- **team_controls_paraphrase**: Shoulder, elbow and wrist provide multiple positioning coordinates. Team describes coupled dynamics, optimized collision-constrained paths and intake avoidance. Locator: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-6328-mechanical-advantage-2023-build-thread/420691/58
- **pinned_code_inspection**: IntakeCubeHandoff runs intake and gripper while moving the arm to CUBE_HANDOFF, then requests HOMED on termination. This verifies coordination logic, not successful physical transfer. Locator: https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeCubeHandoff.java
- **team_service_paraphrase**: Team moved wiring outside the arm to ease tube replacement, accepting exposure with protective wrapping; it reports a short repair list despite electrical complexity. Locator: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-6328-mechanical-advantage-2023-build-thread/420691/209

## Piece flow

For the inspected cube-handoff command: ground cube → dedicated cube intake → overlap with gripper at an arm handoff pose → arm-carried cube → scoring release. The command coordinates intake, arm and gripper; it does not by itself prove compression, transfer sensor coverage, success rate or the full cone route.

## Physical arrangement and swept space

The arm base must carry shoulder reactions; the elbow and wrist sweep through a large changing workspace. The separate intake consumes a ground-access region that can conflict with the arm trajectory. Wiring must survive joint motion and remain replaceable. Exact package coordinates, loaded inertias, pickup mouth width and battery removal route are not established by this selected review.

## Independent motions and powered functions

Shoulder, elbow and wrist are three positioning coordinates. The cube intake and gripper add powered functions; their deployment and transport must be audited before giving a whole-robot DOF or motor total. High moment of inertia is an owner concern; actual loaded inertia is not measured here.

## Burdens avoided

An articulated arm can reach multiple positions without forcing the chassis to follow one fixed mast line. A dedicated collector can decouple a generous ground-capture mouth from the smaller placing hand. These are potential advantages that a fixed-lift alternative must explicitly match.

## Burdens retained

Multiple joint states require calibration, safe transit paths, dynamic control and recovery from interrupted motion. A handoff adds possession transfer, support and timing requirements. The wiring tradeoff shows service access and impact protection can conflict. More complexity is not proof of poor reliability; retain the team repair report as counterevidence.

## Engineering hypothesis

An arm is worthwhile when its workspace and acquisition advantages save more complete-cycle time or failures than its coordination costs create. For a team whose required poses fit a fixed mast, that flexibility may be unnecessary expense. Compare reachable task sets before comparing mechanism prestige.

## Rival explanation

Better control software can make extra coordinates fast and consistent, and a well-developed handoff may outperform direct narrow-mouth pickup. Alliance outcomes cannot isolate architecture from execution or partners.

## When the preference reverses

Prefer articulation if the fixed mast cannot legally reach essential poses, requires slow repositioning, or loses acquisition reliability. Prefer the fixed lift when it meets the same task envelope and measured cycle targets with lower development/service burden.

## Unknowns

Actual inertia, comparable complete-cycle distributions, full cone route, failure recovery behavior, exact event-installed code and final mechanical configuration. Code execution was not simulated or hardware tested.

## Proposed check; not performed

Map identical task poses, legal extensions and intake clearances. Estimate masses and arm inertias from real geometry instead of adjectives. Compare acquisition, handoff and scoring times separately, then combine them with failures; inspect interruption recovery in code before any physical trial.

## Outcome evidence

No controlled architecture comparison or individual cycle-time measurement performed.

## Sources

- https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-6328-mechanical-advantage-2023-build-thread/420691/58
- https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-6328-mechanical-advantage-2023-build-thread/420691/209
- https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2023/blob/1759ecc7ab5d76fcca157d8b76ead233ecb1454f/src/main/java/org/littletonrobotics/frc2023/commands/IntakeCubeHandoff.java

source_reviews.title: Cube handoff command
source_reviews.facts: Collector runs as a deadline while the arm moves to the cube handoff preset and gripper runs. The arm is sent home on command completion.
source_reviews.limitations: Code establishes the intended command sequence. It does not measure successful transfer or establish every event binary.

source_reviews.title: Direct floor sweep command
source_reviews.locator: Height, front/back range and initialize/execute/end branches
source_reviews.facts: The direct mode can follow an arm path toward a floor pickup, then vary the horizontal target along a low sweep while the gripper runs.
source_reviews.limitations: Targets are software coordinates. They do not certify clearances or capture dimensions.

source_reviews.title: Separate cube collector subsystem
source_reviews.facts: Software has separate deploy and roller behavior, initializes the relative angle from the absolute sensor, and profiles deployment.
source_reviews.limitations: Values are tunable defaults, not proof of a particular deployment or installed calibration.

source_reviews.title: Gripper subsystem
source_reviews.facts: Intake uses a timed velocity-based sequence and returns to holding voltage. Different eject requests and high-temperature protection exist.
source_reviews.limitations: A roller speed change does not independently confirm proper seating. No measured false-positive rate.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Mechanical Advantage’s released 2023 software exposes two distinct floor-acquisition paths. The arm can place its own gripper near a piece and sweep along the floor. It can also move into a preset that receives a cube from a separate collector. The extra collector can widen the useful driving approach while the arm provides greater pose freedom at the grid. The cost is an additional transfer, more states to coordinate and a moving arm envelope that matters during transit. That makes 6328 a substantive comparison with 1746: both can retain a piece in the final hand, while their main routes do not have the same approach and transfer costs.
piece_flow: For a direct sweep, the arm follows a path to a low pickup pose. The operator can change horizontal reach while the gripper remains active.
For the separate cube route, the collector runs while the arm moves to the receiving preset and the gripper runs. The cube crosses from collector contact into the final gripper.
The final tool carries the piece through the arm path to the target. The gripper uses an eject profile appropriate to the selected objective.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: An articulated arm trades a compact constrained stroke for several ways to place the tool. Its path must clear the chassis and grid in intermediate poses, not just endpoints. The collector adds a folded volume near the floor and a receiving pose that must align collector discharge with the gripper. Where the hand reaches back across the chassis, cables and tool contents may establish a larger occupied volume than the bare arm links.

subsystems.name: Ground cube collector
subsystems.construction: Independent deployed collector and powered roller are represented in the released code. Deployment is profiled and zeroed using absolute and relative angle information.
subsystems.operation: Drive into a cube with the collector deployed and present it near the gripper.
subsystems.team_rationale: The release documents a dedicated route alongside direct pickup. It does not provide a controlled comparison of the two.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A wider collector can improve approach tolerance, but a cube sent out skewed still needs to be recoverable at the receiver. The same alignment question moves from driver-to-mouth to collector-to-hand.
subsystems.interfaces: Collector pivot, roller outlet and receiving gripper pose must align while the chassis and arm may be moving.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check for cube corners that stick at the exit and for false stow following impact.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact contact widths, loaded transfer speed and event-specific hardware not established by the code.

subsystems.name: Arm reach and sweep
subsystems.construction: The released arm interfaces command preplanned poses and direct tool targets. The floor sweep varies horizontal reach while holding a low target height.
subsystems.operation: Approach the floor pose, sweep for acquisition and return home on command termination.
subsystems.team_rationale: The direct route offers another acquisition option without routing every piece through the cube collector.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: More reach and orientation freedom can save chassis repositioning. Evaluate the price in moving inertia and slower transition margins with the tool loaded.
subsystems.interfaces: The direct sweep needs space outside the frame and a path back from both front and rear.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check whether a pose is available near a wall after a bump or steering error. Test blocked path recovery with the piece retained.
subsystems.unknowns: Setpoint limits do not establish reachable physical contact under load.

subsystems.name: Handoff coordination
subsystems.construction: The collector is the deadline for concurrent arm and gripper commands. The arm targets the cube handoff preset and an indicator marks readiness.
subsystems.operation: Keep the receiver active during transfer, then command the arm to return toward home when the operation ends.
subsystems.team_rationale: The command comments specify an immediate cube handoff.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The design benefits from overlapping motions, so handoff time is not automatically the sum of both actuator times. Still test early arrival, late arrival, interrupted input and asymmetric compression.
subsystems.interfaces: The collector-to-gripper gap, vertical approach and roller direction all affect whether the cube remains controlled through the interface.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: An interrupted command can leave a piece between contacts. Verify a recovery or clear-out route that does not force the arm through an occupied region.
subsystems.unknowns: The software does not establish transfer completion probability or all clearance assumptions.

subsystems.name: Gripper and scoring release
subsystems.construction: Motor-driven gripper with holding, intake and multiple eject requests. The code monitors roller speed and temperature.
subsystems.operation: Intake until the timed velocity sequence concludes, then hold. Choose an eject behavior based on the scoring objective.
subsystems.team_rationale: Separate release settings fit different scoring interactions.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Speed-based detection is available even without an extra detector, but friction, an obstruction and true possession can all slow a roller. Verify which signals remain reliable after wear.
subsystems.interfaces: The gripper shares position targets with the articulated arm, and its own operating state determines whether the game piece will stay put during transit.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: The release includes high-temperature protection. Compare retention after a protective stop and after a stalled attempt.
subsystems.unknowns: No measured possession accuracy, scoring reliability or installed friction coefficients.

revisions: All code observations refer to one pinned release snapshot.
Separate collector and direct floor sweep are distinct operating paths in the same source.
transferable_principles: Compare the entire approach-to-score distribution when choosing a wide intake plus transfer versus direct capture.
Add explicit recovery states for a piece stopped between two mechanisms.
Count each controlled degree of freedom and each possession handoff separately.
disconfirming_conditions: A simpler one-tool path wins if its floor and scoring approach covers the actual field tasks with enough tolerance.
A separate pickup earns the transfer if it cuts approach time and poor pickups enough to pay for its mechanical and control burden.
remaining_gaps: As-built structural dimensions and competition configuration map, capture and transfer success distributions, measured moving inertia and loaded sweep clearances.
